sources.entry: React Native for Ubuntu - Build Ubuntu desktop apps using React Native. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/CanonicalLtd/react-native) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A fork-style copy of the React Native framework from CanonicalLtd, listed on awesome-mac as a way to build Ubuntu desktop apps with React Native, though the README itself is the generic upstream React Native README.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes React Native as a framework for building native application experiences on platforms using JavaScript and React. It states supported operating systems as Android 4.1 (API 16) and iOS 7.0 or later. It points to a Getting Started guide, a tutorial, a UIExplorer example project, and a Documentation section covering Guides, Components, APIs and Polyfills. It also includes instructions for running example apps on iOS via Xcode and on Android via Gradle and a packager script. The README does not mention Ubuntu or desktop support; that claim comes only from the awesome-mac listing description.
use_cases: build cross-platform mobile apps with JavaScript
learn React Native with example projects
run React Native examples on iOS or Android
extend React Native with native modules
build Ubuntu desktop apps with React Native (per listing description)
how_to_run: iOS: open an example's .xcodeproj in Xcode and press Run
Android: install the Android NDK, then run ./gradlew :Examples:Movies:android:app:installDebug
Start the packager with ./packager/packager.sh in a separate shell
Open the Movies app in an emulator
notable: Learn-once, write-anywhere approach using JavaScript and React
UIExplorer example project showing built-in components
Native Modules and Native UI Components guides for extending native functionality
Ships a packager script for running examples on Android
caveats: Supported platforms in the README are Android 4.1+ and iOS 7.0+; no desktop platform is documented
README says the project is under active development, so upgrades may be needed
Examples require Xcode for iOS and the Android NDK for Android
summary.license: BSD (React is BSD licensed with an additional patent grant; examples and some components are separately licensed)
